ownership_reason: Only the gold walks the tree and decides, node by node, whether to record a declared name and whether to enter a node's children; hops 1-4 hold the root of the branch and the map and get the filled map back, and a nested function's var, once recorded under its name, cannot be told apart from a var of the branch by any caller, and it keeps a later declaration of the same name in the branch itself from being recorded (first declaration wins), so removing entries afterwards cannot restore the branch's own var. The convention is pinned outside the gold: SyntacticScopeCreator.scanVars declares a function's name and does not examine the function's children, and SyntacticScopeCreatorTest.testFunctionScope asserts that y in '[function bar2() { var y; }]' is not declared in the global scope; the facade's production caller NodeUtil.redeclareVarsInsideBranch redeclares 'the VAR declarations in that tree that are not in an inner scope', and FoldConstantsTest.testVarLifting lifts only 'var a' out of 'if(false)var a=function(){var b};'; the facade's own javadoc says 'excluding descent scopes'. The gold's javadoc promises the vars declared in a branch, which foo, a var of the anonymous function in 'function(){var foo;}', is not. A one-line loop at hop 4 that calls the gold only for the root's children that are not functions passes the existing tests but still enters a function one block deeper, so it does not deliver hop 4's documented result.
